title: 6.9 Polar Equations of Conics

icans: I can find the eccentricity of a conic from its polar equation and identify it.
I can find the vertices of a conic in polar form.
I can write the polar equation of a conic.

vocab: e: the ratio of a point’s distance to the focus and its distance to the ____________
the fixed line used with the focus to __________ a conic

blocks.p: Graph r = e/(1 − e cos θ) with a slider for e.

blocks.sec: Part 2 · Notes and examples (fill in each note, then work the example)

notes: Polar conics: r = ep/(1 ± e cos θ) or r = ep/(1 ± e sin θ): ellipse if e < 1, parabola if e = 1, hyperbola if e _______________ 1.
Reading e: first rewrite so the denominator starts with _______________.

blocks.stem: Identify the conic r = 15/(3 − 2 cos θ).
Identify r = 32/(3 + 5 sin θ) and find its vertices.

notes: Directrix: cos θ means a vertical directrix (x = ±p); sin θ means a _______________ directrix (y = ±p).

blocks.stem: Write the polar equation of the parabola with focus at the pole and directrix y = 3.
Find the eccentricity and vertices of r = 6/(2 + cos θ).
Write the polar equation of the ellipse with e = 1/2, focus at the pole, and directrix x = 4.

tickets.stem: Find the eccentricity of r = 4/(1 − 3 cos θ) and identify the conic.
Is the directrix of r = 2/(1 − sin θ) vertical or horizontal?
